narrative: 过肩镜头是自带空间粘合剂的默认对话覆盖方式。即使画面拉近，对话伙伴依然在物理上“在场”。
肩膀的大小以及它遮挡画面的程度，可以让观者感到强势、亲密，或者被困住。当你需要把某人孤立出来，仿佛另一个人已经离开了房间时，过肩镜头就不是合适的工具——那应该用干净的单人镜头（Single）。
如果两张脸都同样清晰、同样完整，它也不是合适的工具——那是双人镜头（Two-Shot）。过肩镜头是一种取景选择。
正反打（Shot/reverse shot）是一种剪辑模式。两者不是同义词。
how: 把摄影机放在一个人的身侧，越过一个虚化的近处肩膀，看向远处的脸。远处的人望向近处的人，也就是望向那个肩膀，绝不看向镜头。
反打镜头要匹配前景人物的位置、头部大小和视线方向。180度线就是两个人之间的那条轴线。
过肩镜头的覆盖始终停留在这条轴线的同一侧。如果近处的肩膀在画面右侧，远处的脸就应望向画面右侧方向。
反打的过肩镜头会换成另一个人在近处，但依然停留在轴线的同一侧，这样银幕方向就不会翻转。在这种覆盖方式里，越轴不是一种风格选择——它会让两个人看起来像坐在同一条长椅上，而不是在对话。
用焦点和布光让说话的脸保持清晰，近处的衣物保持虚化。提示词：Over-the-shoulder framing of [Subject], near shoulder soft in foreground, the far face sharp, looking toward the near shoulder, 180-line held.
永远不要越过180度线。在两人之间画出这条轴线，让摄影机始终待在轴线的一侧。远处的脸望向近处的肩膀，反打镜头也停留在轴线的同一侧。如果他们看向镜头，或者彼此看向相反方向，那就不再是过肩镜头的覆盖方式了。
when: 当你希望这段关系一直留在画面里时，把它当作默认的对话覆盖方式：一间餐馆、一场取证问询、一场隔着玻璃的访谈。不要在反打镜头里让肩膀大小不匹配，也不要把干净的单人镜头误称为过肩镜头。
vs: 双人镜头让两张脸同时拥有画面的主导权；单人镜头则去掉了前景的对话伙伴——“脏”单人镜头可能会在边缘露出一点身体，但没有真正构图意义上的肩膀锚点。
反应镜头（Reaction Shot）既可以用过肩镜头的方式拍，也可以用单人镜头的方式拍。过肩镜头的定义是：近处的身体碎片，远处的脸作为主体。
examples_film: 《社交网络》（The Social Network）用这种构图逻辑来处理对峙和取证问询的场景。《盗火线》（Heat）的餐馆戏在双人镜头和更贴近的镜头之间，用共享的空间关系和对立的覆盖方式来展开。
《沉默的羔羊》（The Silence of the Lambs）的访谈戏，全靠“谁的肩膀、谁的玻璃、谁的脸”来维系。《斯汤达综合症》（The Stendhal Syndrome）通过交替的视角，把一个人和一幅画连接起来，是一种相近的语法——越过一样东西去看向另一样。
语法：关系依然留在前景里。
mistakes: 最常被搞混的近邻是双人镜头（两张脸都完整）或单人镜头（没有肩膀）。破绽是两个人同样清晰，或者是一张干净的肖像镜头。
更严重的破绽是180度线被打破：远处的人看向镜头，或者看向偏离近处肩膀的方向，导致反打镜头会让两人看起来坐在同一侧。解决办法：一个虚化的肩膀，一张望向那个肩膀方向的清晰的脸，匹配的反打镜头，守住这条轴线。

faq.q: What is Over-the-Shoulder Coverage in film?
faq.a: 过肩镜头把远处的人当作主体来取景，同时用近处的肩膀或头部为前景提供锚点。成对出现的过肩镜头，即便我们贴近拍一张脸，也能让两个人始终共享同一个空间逻辑。
单人镜头是一个主要人物，没有对话伙伴占据前景。过肩镜头则把近处的肩膀或头部作为空间上的粘合剂留在画面里。如果另一个人已经从这个矩形画面里消失了，那就是单人镜头，即使他仍然在房间里。

faq.q: When should I use Over-the-Shoulder Coverage?
faq.a: 用于那些应该让关系在物理上保持存在的对话。当孤立感才是重点时不要用它，也不要在反打镜头里出现不匹配。

faq.q: How do I prompt Over-the-Shoulder Coverage for AI image or video?
faq.a: 写：Over-the-shoulder framing of [Subject], near shoulder soft in foreground, the far face sharp, looking toward the near shoulder。点名谁在近处，守住180度线。对于视频，生成一个在同一侧轴线上匹配的反打镜头作为第二个镜头，而不是把摄影机绕到他们身后。

faq.q: Does an over-the-shoulder shot break the 180-degree rule?
faq.a: 不会。正确的过肩镜头正是你守住180度线的方式。摄影机始终停留在两人之间那条轴线的一侧。远处的脸望向近处的肩膀，而不是看向镜头。越过那条线会让银幕方向翻转，这是一个覆盖错误，而不是一种风格。

narrative: OTS is default dialogue coverage with spatial glue. The partner remains physically present even in a close view.

Shoulder size and how much it obstructs can make the observer feel dominant, intimate, or trapped. It is the wrong tool when you need to isolate someone as if the other person had left the room: that is a clean single.
It is also the wrong tool if both faces are equally sharp and complete: that is a two-shot. An over-the-shoulder shot is a framing choice.
Shot/reverse shot is an editing pattern. They are not synonyms.
how: Place the camera beside one body, looking past a soft near shoulder at the far face. The far person looks at the near person, toward that shoulder, never into the lens.
Match foreground body position, head size, and eyeline on the reverse. The 180-degree line is the axis between the two bodies.
OTS coverage lives on one side of that line. If the near shoulder sits camera-right, the far face looks camera-right.

The reverse OTS swaps who is near, but it stays on the same side of the axis so screen direction does not flip. Crossing the line is not a style choice in this coverage: it makes two people look like they share a bench instead of a conversation.

Use focus and lighting to keep the speaking face sharp and the near cloth soft. Prompt: Over-the-shoulder framing of [Subject], near shoulder soft in foreground, the far face sharp, looking toward the near shoulder, 180-line held.

Never cross the 180-degree line. Draw the axis between the two people and keep the camera on one side of it. Far face looks at the near shoulder. The reverse stays on the same side of the axis. If they look into the lens or away from each other, it is no longer OTS coverage.
when: Use it as default dialogue coverage when you want the relationship to stay in the picture: a diner, a deposition, an interview through glass. Do not mismatch shoulder size on the reverse, and do not call a clean single an OTS.
vs: A Two-Shot gives both faces authorship. A Single removes the foreground partner; a dirty single may chew the edge without a true shoulder anchor.
A Reaction Shot may be taken as OTS or as a single. OTS means: near body fragment, far face subject.
examples_film: The Social Network runs confrontations and depositions in this geometry. Heat 's diner uses shared geography and opposing coverage between the two-shot and the tighter work.

The Silence of the Lambs interviews live on whose shoulder, whose glass, whose face. The Stendhal Syndrome connects a person and a painting through alternating views, related grammar of looking past one thing at another.
Grammar: relation still in the foreground.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a Two-Shot (both faces complete) or a Single (no shoulder). The tell is two people equally sharp, or a clean portrait.

The worse tell is a broken 180: the far person looks into the lens or away from the near shoulder, so the reverse would make them appear to sit on the same side. Fix: one soft shoulder, one sharp face looking at that shoulder, matched reverse, line held.

faq.q: What is Over-the-Shoulder Coverage in film?
faq.a: Over-the-shoulder coverage frames the far person as the subject while a near shoulder or head anchors the foreground. Paired OTS shots keep two people in a shared geometry even when we are close on one face.

A single is one principal with no partner owning the foreground. OTS keeps a near shoulder or head in frame as a spatial glue. If the other person is gone from the rectangle, you have a single, even if they are still in the room.

faq.q: When should I use Over-the-Shoulder Coverage?
faq.a: Use it for dialogue that should keep the relationship physically present. Do not use it when isolation is the point, and do not mismatch the reverse.

faq.q: How do I prompt Over-the-Shoulder Coverage for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write Over-the-shoulder framing of [Subject], near shoulder soft in foreground, the far face sharp, looking toward the near shoulder. Name who is near. Hold the 180. For video, generate a matched reverse as a second shot on the same side of the line, rather than spinning the camera around them.

faq.q: Does an over-the-shoulder shot break the 180-degree rule?
faq.a: No. A correct OTS is how you hold the 180. The camera stays on one side of the line between the two people. The far face looks toward the near shoulder, not into the lens. Crossing that line flips screen direction and is a coverage error, not a look.
